lead: WinPmem saves the physical memory (RAM) of a running Windows computer to a file. It is a small command-line program that loads a driver to read memory.
use_when: You need a copy of RAM from a running Windows computer before it is switched off.
You want a raw memory image to analyse with a memory tool.
You need a small tool that runs from a USB stick without other software.

features.title: Memory capture
items: Writes the physical memory to a raw image file
The mini programs include both the 32-bit and 64-bit drivers and load the right one
The driver is unloaded after the capture

features.title: Design
items: Uses a read interface to the driver, and the imaging logic runs in user space
This allows copying over a network, hashing and live analysis
The project describes three independent ways to read memory, two of which give a complete dump

features.title: Platforms
items: The project lists Windows 7 to Windows 10, 32-bit and 64-bit
The standalone program needs no other software

features.title: Open source
items: Started at Google and was part of the Rekall project
Is the Windows counterpart of Linpmem

requirements: A Windows computer in the range the project lists (Windows 7 to 10), and rights to load a kernel driver. The README does not say that administrator rights are needed, but loading a driver normally needs them. Save the image to a different drive with enough free space for all the RAM.

steps.title: Get the program
steps.text: Download the WinPmem program from the project's GitHub page. Use the mini version that matches your computer, for example winpmem_mini_x64.exe for 64-bit Windows. Check the file hash against the one you recorded when you downloaded it.

steps.title: Prepare the output drive
steps.text: Use a clean external drive with free space larger than the RAM of the target computer. Do not save the image on the computer's own disk, because that changes the evidence.

steps.title: Plan before you run
steps.text: A memory capture changes the running computer a little, because the program and its driver are loaded. Write down the time, who did it and which tool and version you used. Do this before you run the tool.

steps.title: Show the help
steps.text: Run the program with no arguments to see the usage text for your version.

steps.title: Capture the memory
steps.text: Run the program with the name of the output file. Wait until it finishes and the prompt returns. The README gives this form of the command.

steps.title: Hash and keep the image
steps.text: Calculate a hash of the raw file, write it in your notes and keep the image as read-only evidence. Make a working copy for analysis.

steps.title: Analyse the image
steps.text: Open the raw file in a memory analysis tool such as Volatility 3 or MemProcFS to list processes, network connections and other details.

options.what: Writes a raw image to physmem.raw with the default method.
Uses the MmMapIoSpace method to write a raw image.
Loads the driver with write support. The project warns that this is dangerous and only for self-signed test builds.

cases.title: Malware and intrusion investigations
cases.why: Memory can hold running processes, network connections and code that is never saved to disk.

cases.title: Cases with encrypted drives
cases.why: A memory capture from a running computer may hold material that is not available after shutdown.

cases.title: Incident response triage
cases.why: A small single-file tool is easy to copy to a computer and run quickly.

cases.title: Teaching memory forensics
cases.why: Students can capture RAM from a test virtual machine and then practise with a memory analysis tool.

strengths: Small program, no extra software needed.
Simple command: one program name and one output file name.
Imaging in user space allows hashing and copying over a network.
limits: It writes raw images only. The mini programs cannot write AFF4 files.
The README lists Windows 7 to 10. Check that it works on your Windows version before an important case, and test on a lab computer.
The README notes that reads can fail for physical addresses above half the maximum 64-bit value. This is unlikely, but possible as RAM grows.
It loads a kernel driver, so security software may block it. Test this in advance on a lab computer.
It does not analyse memory. You need a tool such as Volatility 3.
The README is short. Test the tool on a lab computer and read the project's pages for newer versions.
